chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah ibn A'yan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

God the Exalted made prayer obligatory, and the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) established it in ten forms: the prayer of the resident and the traveler, the prayer of fear in three forms, the eclipse prayer for the sun and the moon, the prayer of the two Eids, the prayer for rain, and the prayer over the dead.
ai.seo_question: What are the ten types of prayers in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* establishes the comprehensive legal framework for salat by enumerating ten distinct forms, emphasizing the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) role in detailing the divine command. It highlights the flexibility of Islamic jurisprudence, accommodating varying states such as travel, fear, and celestial phenomena, while also addressing communal needs like rain and funeral rites. This classification underscores the holistic nature of worship in Shia tradition, integrating personal devotion with social and cosmic dimensions.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 10-40 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Yaqoob ibn Yazid, on the authority of Hammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Hurayz, on the authority of Zurarah ibn A’ayan that Abi Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB) said,

“The Honorable the Exalted God made prayers incumbent and God’s Prophet (MGB) established ten forms of it. These are praying while staying somewhere; praying while on a journey; praying due to fear on three occasions; praying for the eclipse of the Sun; praying for the eclipse of the moon; praying on the two Holy Eids; praying for rain; and praying over the dead.”
